title: AI helped – but it still took 12 months. My roguelite and async PvP tower defense launches on Steam in 4 days.
author: JourneyTD_Dev
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev! Nice to meet you guys! I'm Chris, and I've been building **Journey TD** solo – a roguelite tower defense that started as my love letter to the old Warcraft 3 TD maps like YouTD. It launches on Steam on **November 11**. I can't draw myself, so AI played a big part in getting here – but it was still 12 months of work. And a lot of the art is hand-drawn by my art designer, like the Steam store banners, the loading screens and the character portraits in the tutorial. Here's how it all fit in – and below that, what the game actually is.

**How AI fit into making it**

* **Code:** Godot 4 and GDScript, built with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). I'm the designer and director: I decide what gets built, playtest it and send it back until it feels right.
* **Pixel art:** AI (PixelLab) gives me a starting point. I generate a few versions, keep the one that fits best next to the rest, and my art designer and I are reworking the sprites by hand in Aseprite, piece by piece.
* **Not AI:** the design and balancing decisions (shaped by a lot of playtesting with our Discord beta testers) and all the hand-drawn art. Nothing in the game is generated while you play.

**Three things that made the biggest difference**

1. **Content as data.** Every tower, enemy and map is its own data file, and abilities are small reusable building blocks. A new tower is mostly a new file instead of a change to the core code – so every AI change stays small and easy to check.
2. **Write things down.** Each system has a short design note that the AI reads before it starts and updates when it's done, plus automated tests for every system. With 168 towers, that's what stops old features from quietly breaking.
3. **Judge art in the game.** I don't approve a sprite on its own – only in the game, next to its neighbours, and usually out of five versions. Consistency beats any single great image.

**The core of a run**

* Your towers are the maze – enemies always take the shortest route, so every placement matters
* You draft your towers each run and build around what you get – 168 towers across five elements (plus a sixth you'll have to find), each with its own abilities
* Merge three identical towers into a stronger one
* Power-up drafts, boss waves, and a black market for potions
* At fixed waves a DPS Arena tests your build – your total damage decides the loot chest

**Every map plays differently**

* The Forest is the classic: a winding river, bridges and a cliff plateau – rolled into a new layout every run
* The Graveyard has a Wheel of the Dead that spins blessings and curses onto your elements
* In the Desert a Djinn curses you – and lets you gamble your way out (1% jackpot\^\^)

**Between runs**

* Gear up your builder with loot (rarities, affixes, refining, salvaging) and grow a skill tree
* Socket 27 ultra-rare power runes
* Collect a card for every tower in your album
* 380+ achievements that unlock titles and skins

**For the competitive ones**

* 150 waves, 300 waves or Endless, six difficulties – and a seventh for anyone who thinks that's not enough
* Leaderboards for every map, mode and difficulty, plus a live score band that races your own best run
* Colosseum: everyone plays the same seed, map and elements each week – fight for the top 100
* Supremacy: same idea, but your whole progression counts

If it looks like your kind of game, a wishlist before launch helps a lot: [Journey TD on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5084410/Journey_TD/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=r_aigamedev)  
Also, if you'd like to join our Discord community, you're very welcome: [https://discord.com/invite/JsK7ZxrYuF](https://discord.com/invite/JsK7ZxrYuF)

Cheers and good luck with your projects,  
Chris
